scope: Software supply-chain controls and Solana client/indexing compatibility
method: Official repositories/documentation checked for selected sources. No installation, secret scan, REA run, code change, build or live-chain test was performed.

provenance: Official Semgrep repository and documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Static analysis platform supports rule-based code scanning across supported languages.
Custom rules can encode repository-specific unsafe patterns.
patterns: Add focused rules for accidental signer imports or unsafe live-trading bypasses.
Run scans in CI and review findings rather than treating a clean scan as a proof.
overlap: Complements deterministic tests and code review; does not replace them.
risks: Rule coverage and false positives vary.
Hosted scanning requires code/data access review.
validation: Test each custom rule against positive and negative fixtures.
Pin scanner/rule versions and retain output.

provenance: Official StrykerJS repository and documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Mutation testing evaluates whether tests detect deliberately introduced code changes.
Mutation score indicates test sensitivity for generated mutations, not correctness of requirements.
patterns: Use mutation testing selectively on feed health and authorization predicates.
Inspect surviving mutations as missing assertions or equivalent transformations.
overlap: Strengthens existing deterministic tests without adding a runtime engine.
risks: Mutation runs can be resource-intensive.
A high score can still miss unmodeled behaviors.
validation: Start with a narrow critical module set and deterministic test setup.
Review each survivor and document exclusions.

discoveries: Automated dependency update tool can open reviewable update pull requests.
Configuration supports update scheduling and grouping across package ecosystems.
patterns: Create small dependency update PRs with lockfile and changelog evidence.
Separate security updates from routine version updates.
overlap: Automation prepares updates; it should not auto-merge dependencies into an execution system.
risks: Unreviewed update PRs can change behavior or introduce malicious packages.
Private registry access requires credential scoping.
validation: Require build/tests and diff review before merge.
Pin Renovate config and restrict permissions.

discoveries: Cosign supports signing and verifying container images and blobs.
README recommends verifying image digests and explicitly checking signer identity/issuer for keyless signatures.
patterns: Bind release verification to artifact digest and expected workflow identity.
Retain verification bundle and provenance with release evidence.
overlap: Would protect artifact provenance, not market data or runtime decisions.
risks: Signing identity and trust-root management are security-critical.
Transparency records can expose signer identity metadata.
validation: Verify valid, wrong-identity, changed-digest and expired/trust-root cases.
Document offline verification inputs.

provenance: Official Rekor repository/OpenAPI and Sigstore architecture documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Rekor provides a transparency log for signed software artifacts.
Transparency logs are append-only and should store verifiable signing records/digests, not sensitive payloads.
patterns: Record artifact digests and signed build attestations for release auditability.
Verify inclusion/checkpoint evidence independently.
overlap: Supply-chain provenance only; it does not certify runtime safety.
risks: Append-only entries cannot be removed and may expose metadata.
Rekor v1 API material and newer implementations differ; pin protocol/version.
validation: Test inclusion and signature verification using public test artifacts.
Avoid placing secrets or private user data into transparency entries.

provenance: Official Trivy vulnerability scanner documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Trivy scans OS, language package and other targets for known vulnerabilities.
Scanner databases are fetched/cached and their freshness affects findings.
patterns: Scan source dependencies and release images in CI.
Track database timestamp and distinguish vulnerabilities from exploitability assessment.
overlap: Complements code and dependency review, not a substitute for it.
risks: Scanner database may be stale or omit issues.
Container scanning scope depends on target and configuration.
validation: Use known vulnerable/safe fixtures and verify expected results.
Pin scanner version and database/update policy.

discoveries: Scans supported dependency manifests against OSV vulnerability data.
The repository distinguishes v2 from legacy v1 workflows; CLI and output should be pinned.
patterns: Include dependency scans in CI with machine-readable outputs.
Review direct and transitive dependency advisories before updating.
overlap: Supply-chain hygiene only; no runtime code-path role.
risks: Advisory matching can have package/version ambiguity.
Scanner major version changes can alter output and behavior.
validation: Test against known vulnerable lockfiles and clean fixtures.
Record scanner version and database timestamp.

provenance: Official Gitleaks repository and documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Secret scanner detects credential-like patterns in files and Git history.
Custom rules and allowlists affect detection coverage.
patterns: Run local/CI secret scans and prevent newly introduced credential patterns.
Treat matches as sensitive incident evidence and redact reports.
overlap: Can detect accidental exposure, but cannot revoke or rotate a credential.
risks: False positives and allowlists can hide real secrets.
Scanner output itself may include matched secret material.
validation: Test known dummy secrets and false-positive fixtures.
Protect scan artifacts and review allowlist changes.

provenance: Official OPA README and documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: OPA evaluates declarative Rego policies against caller-supplied data.
Integrations require the application to enforce returned allow/deny decisions.
patterns: Express release/deployment guardrails as tested policies.
Keep signer authorization enforced in existing trusted code, even if policy evaluation is externalized.
overlap: Potential policy tooling, but not a replacement for existing capital/signing controls.
risks: Policy data/context omissions can produce unsafe allows.
Networked policy service availability must fail closed where critical.
validation: Test allow/deny boundary cases and policy bundle integrity.
Prove failure or timeout cannot bypass execution authority.

provenance: Official CodeQL query/library repository README; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Repository contains standard CodeQL libraries and queries used for code security analysis.
The CodeQL CLI/engine is separately licensed from this open source query repository.
patterns: Use supported code scanning for source-level security queries in CI.
Add custom queries only with reviewed test fixtures.
overlap: Static analysis complements tests; repository alone does not supply all scanning components or licensing.
risks: CLI licensing differs from query repo license.
Static findings require triage and do not prove absence of vulnerabilities.
validation: Verify code language support and entitlement before use.
Test custom query expected matches and non-matches.
sources.license: Query repo MIT; CLI/engine separately licensed (README)

provenance: Official Solana Program Library Token-2022 repository and docs; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Token-2022 program supports extensions that alter token-account or mint behavior.
Integrators need to inspect enabled extensions rather than assume legacy SPL Token semantics.
The canonical TransferFee.calculate_fee uses ceiling division for fractional raw units, then caps the result at maximum_fee; floor-based calculations understate some fees.
patterns: Parse token program ID and extension state before modeling transfer semantics.
Use checked arithmetic and explicit transfer-fee accounting where applicable.
Mirror the canonical ceil-rounding and maximum-fee cap with raw-unit boundary fixtures.
overlap: Extends existing token compatibility; no broad integration without extension-specific needs.
risks: Unsupported extensions can invalidate quote, transfer or net-PnL assumptions.
Program upgrades and SDK versions require pinning.
validation: Build fixtures for supported/unsupported extension combinations.
Compare quote, simulation and confirmed transfer amounts.
Test fractional one-unit fees, maximum-fee caps, zero and 10000 bps against pinned Token-2022 semantics.

provenance: Official Blockdaemon AccountsDB Kafka plugin repository; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Validator AccountsDB plugin exports account updates to Kafka.
It is infrastructure-side account streaming, distinct from ordinary client RPC polling.
patterns: Preserve slot, write version and account identity in streamed records.
Use consumer checkpoints and gap reconciliation for restart recovery.
overlap: Alternative upstream data transport; overlaps at the account-event ingestion boundary.
risks: Requires validator/plugin access and Kafka operations.
Account update delivery alone may not supply full transaction semantics.
validation: Test ordering, duplicate, disconnect and restart behavior on isolated fixtures.
Reconcile sampled account state against canonical RPC reads.

provenance: Official Solana Foundation solana-web3.js repository; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Current repository describes a v3+ pnpm workspace, while legacy v1.x is on a maintenance branch with critical fixes only.
Packages are independently versioned; root workspace is orchestration rather than the published client package.
patterns: Pin exact client major/version and test RPC serialization behavior.
Treat migration between v1 and v3 as an explicit compatibility project.
overlap: Client SDK choice must align with existing interfaces; avoid duplicate Solana client abstraction without a concrete migration need.
risks: Major version behavior and types may differ.
Incompatible transaction serialization can break signing/fee accounting.
validation: Test transaction/message serialization, RPC errors and versioned transaction fixtures.
Keep signer/custody restrictions unchanged during any upgrade.

provenance: Official Meteora DBC SDK repository and developer guide; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: SDK targets Meteora Dynamic Bonding Curve launch pools, quoting/trading helpers and migration lifecycle.
Official developer guide describes migration of completed DBC pools to DAMM v2 and separate program/account flows.
patterns: Model launch state and graduation destination explicitly per mint/pool.
Keep quote math and lifecycle transitions versioned by program/SDK revision.
overlap: Adds venue-specific lifecycle coverage to existing AMM bridge; avoid generic assumptions that every token graduates to one venue.
risks: Program IDs, account layouts, fees and migration behavior can change.
Transfer hooks/extensions may affect executable quotes.
validation: Use official fixtures/program IDs and test lifecycle transitions on local/test environments.
Compare SDK quote results with on-chain simulation and confirmed amounts.

provenance: Official Carbon repository and documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Carbon is an indexing framework for decoding Solana transactions/accounts into data pipelines.
Decoders and datasource transports are composable, so versioned program decoders can be isolated.
patterns: Use independently tested decoders per program and retain raw event provenance.
Separate ingestion transport from protocol-specific decoding.
overlap: Conceptually overlaps the current canonical ingress and decoders; adopt patterns, not a parallel ingestion engine.
risks: Decoder coverage may lag protocol changes.
Third-party index outputs are not canonical state without reconciliation.
validation: Test decoders with captured versioned transactions and malformed inputs.
Compare decoded events to RPC/account state and source receipts.
